sections.h2: Where does the Greene County Recorder work, and until when?
sections.html:
Find the office on the third floor of 69 Greene St. in Xenia. The recorder's page posts two sets of hours on weekdays: the counter is staffed until 4:00 p.m., while recording itself stops at 3:00 p.m. After that, expect a deed to sit until the following business day.

Permanent land records for the whole county live here. The published list of filings is long, and a seller will touch several of these during a sale:

  • Deeds, mortgages and releases of mortgage
  • Easements, leases and land contracts
  • Affidavits, trusts and powers of attorney
  • Mechanic's liens, federal tax liens and child support liens
  • Plats, condominium documents and annexations

The office also files and certifies military discharges. Those are closed to the public, and the veteran or heirs can ask for a copy free of charge.

sections.h2: What has to happen before a Greene County deed is recorded?
sections.html:
Stop at the auditor first. The transfer page there asks for a finished Statement of Value (DTE 100) or the exempt version (DTE 100 EX), fees payable to the auditor, a grantor name spelled as in the grantor's own deed, and map department initials. The grantor signs, and a notary acknowledges the signature.

R.C. 5301.01 names the officials who may take that acknowledgment, from notaries and mayors to court clerks, auditors and engineers. Recording protects the buyer as well. Under R.C. 5301.25, a deed left unrecorded counts as fraudulent toward a later purchaser who bought in good faith without notice of it.

Land in the CAUV farm program, in the filing year or the year before, needs that program's conveyance statement attached. If a survey was made, the deed has to carry the surveyor's name.

sections.h2: What will recording a deed cost in Greene County?
sections.html:
R.C. 317.32 sets the schedule, and every charge pairs a base amount with a matching housing trust fund amount. Senate Bill 94 opened the door to as much as $5.00 more per document, yet a January 2, 2026 notice from the Greene County Recorder says standard fees stay unchanged.

Recording fees printed in R.C. 317.32 (base plus housing trust fund)
ItemBase feeHousing trust fund fee
Record and index, first two pages$17$17
Each added page$4$4
Marginal reference by separate instrument$2$2
Certified copy, per page$1$1
Document preservation surchargeUp to $5None listed

Copies are cheaper when you make them yourself: $.10 a page for self-service official copies versus $2.00 a page when staff do it.

sections.h2: Which transfer charges come before recording in Greene County?
sections.html:
The auditor collects these. On its page the county shows a combined $2.00 per thousand dollars of purchase price, built from a $1.00 conveyance fee plus a $1.00 transfer fee, along with $0.50 per parcel. An online calculator is posted.

The grantor owes the tax, and R.C. 322.02 caps a county's own transfer tax at 30 cents per hundred dollars of value. Some transfers carry no fee under R.C. 319.54, including these:

  • Moves among heirs or devisees of one decedent where no money is paid
  • Gifts between spouses or from parent to child
  • Deeds into a revocable trust, and back out to the grantor
  • Deeds given only to secure or release a debt

The reason for the exemption goes on the statement, so review it with the closing agent.

sections.h2: Which liens can show up against a Greene County seller?
sections.html:
The recorder's published list names the liens it files, and a buyer's title company will search for each one against the seller's name and the parcel. Liens on the county's list include mechanic's liens, Medicaid fraud liens, federal tax liens, child support liens, unemployment compensation liens, personal tax liens and workers' compensation liens. A Notice of Commencement is filed here as well.

The Ohio Recorders' Association table gives the fee for several of them, and the amounts differ by type:

  • Federal tax lien (IRS): $5.00, with $3.00 to release it.
  • Unemployment compensation lien and workers' compensation lien: no fee.
  • Personal property tax lien and Medicaid fraud lien: no fee.
  • Mechanic's lien and its release: the standard per-page fee.

A seller who knows of a lien should ask the lienholder for a recorded release before closing day. Once the release is filed, it appears in the same index as the original lien, which lets the title examiner clear the exception.

sections.h2: Which deed forms turn up in Greene County sales?
sections.html:
The state fee table names the usual choices, each recorded at the same per-page rates: warranty, limited warranty, quit claim and survivorship deeds. Estate and trust sales bring executor's, administrator's, guardian's or trustee's deeds, according to who holds authority. A transfer on death designation affidavit appears too.

Survivorship deeds fall under R.C. 5302.20: language showing clear intent creates the tenancy, and a conveyance from every tenant ends it. Co-owners who inherited together should read the recorded deed to see whether they hold in survivorship or in common.

sections.h2: Which communities record deeds in Xenia?
sections.html:
Land is recorded where it sits, so parcels in every city, village and township here go through the Xenia office. Beavercreek, Bellbrook, Fairborn and Xenia are the cities, and Kettering extends into Greene County although most of it is in Montgomery County. The county takes its name from Revolutionary War General Nathanael Greene, and Clark, Madison, Fayette, Clinton, Warren and Montgomery counties touch its borders.

Highways include I-675, I-71, US 35, US 42 and US 68. With more than 73,000 parcels on the auditor's rolls, each parcel has its own chain of recorded documents, and a buyer's title search reads that chain back through earlier deeds. A gap in it can slow a sale.

Public districts here are Beavercreek, Bellbrook-Sugarcreek, Cedar Cliff, Fairborn, Greeneview, Xenia Community and Yellow Springs.

sections.h2: How do you search records and find a mortgage release in Greene County?
sections.html:
Online, the Recorder's Document Search covers filings from 1984 onward. Website images carry a watermark, and a watermarked page cannot be submitted for recording, so pull clean copies at the counter. A transfer tracking table reports where a newly submitted transfer stands, and a fraud alert service can notify an owner when something is filed against a registered property.

A lender gets 90 days after payoff to file the release or satisfaction of mortgage. An owner who cleared a loan long ago should look up that release before listing, since a missing one can stall a closing.

sections.h2: What household numbers does the Census give for Greene County?
sections.html: Greene County had 68,166 households in the 2020 to 2024 survey, averaging 2.38 people, and roughly 74,000 housing units in 2025. Monthly owner costs have a median of $1,702 with a mortgage and $700 without one. Builders pulled 567 permits in 2025, and 92.8 percent of households subscribe to broadband, which helps with online document submissions.

faqs.q: When does Greene County stop recording documents each day?
faqs.a: At 3:00 p.m. on weekdays, with recording starting at 7:30 a.m. The office itself stays open until 4:00 p.m., so bring anything urgent early in the day.

faqs.q: Did Greene County raise recording fees after the state change?
faqs.a: Not for standard documents. A January 2, 2026 recorder notice says fees stay put, although Senate Bill 94 permits up to $5.00 more.

faqs.q: Which office collects the Greene County transfer charge?
faqs.a: The auditor, from the grantor, ahead of recording. Its page lists $2.00 per thousand dollars of price and a $0.50 per-parcel charge.

faqs.q: How do I get a copy of my Greene County deed?
faqs.a: Go to 69 Greene St., third floor, or use the online document search. Self-service official copies cost $.10 a page, and staff-made ones cost $2.00 a page.

faqs.q: How soon must a lender record a mortgage release in Greene County?
faqs.a: Within ninety days of payoff. The recorder holds the release, and copies come from the counter or the document search.
